Tools of the Trade

Three Things To Know About Knowledge Graphs

Knowledge graphs turn relationships into machine-interpretable knowledge — the foundation behind SAP’s context-aware AI, from EKX to Joule.

March 11, 2025 3 min read

Adapted for Future of PMM from Stefanie Glenk’s SAP News primer (Mar 11, 2025). Source

Several SAP AI announcements mention knowledge graphs — a concept that can feel abstract until you need reliable answers about products, processes, or APIs. A knowledge graph turns data into machine-interpretable knowledge by modeling the relationships between objects as a network of interconnected points, not isolated tables.

That relational model is why graphs beat flat databases when you need to evaluate information across departments and systems, understand it in context, and surface hidden connections for a business user.

The three strengths

Why knowledge graphs matter

SAP has been building on knowledge graph experience across Business AI, content, and data platform teams. The key strengths show up the same way for PMM work as they do for product engineering:

  • Enhanced data integration and accessibility — connect disparate sources into one interconnected view so queries span systems instead of stopping at silo boundaries.
  • Scalability and extensibility — graphs grow as requirements change; new sources and capabilities can be added without starting over.
  • Improved business context — semantic linking lets people ask in economic / business terms while AI searches modeled relationships for an answer humans can understand.

PMM framing

When you ask EKX or Joule a product or competitive question, you’re relying on this structure. Graphs are how SAP connects tables, business objects, and processes so Q&A can be holistic — not a lucky paraphrase from a generic model.

Inside SAP

Three groups, one direction

Knowledge graph work at SAP has been driven mainly by three groups — now converging into the unified SAP Knowledge Graph story you see behind EKX and Joule:

  • SAP Business AI — deep data-model layer (tables, fields, views, APIs, entity sets and their relationships), starting with SAP S/4HANA cloud content and expanding toward other LoBs and use cases such as sustainability.
  • SAP Global Content Group (GCG) — enterprise knowledge network of processes, tools, and metrics, already in productive use for contextualized insights and integrated into platforms such as the Business Accelerator Hub Transformation Domain, Signavio Value Accelerator Library, LeanIX, and Signavio Process Explorer (also feeding ProcessAI recommendations).
  • SAP Business Data Cloud (formerly Datasphere) — infrastructure so customers can build their own knowledge graphs that mix SAP and customer knowledge for more accurate AI applications.

Where it leads

An integrated graph for AI that reasons

The long-term goal is a joint knowledge graph spanning technology, tables, business processes, products, and metrics — so queries get more powerful as isolated graphs connect.

“Our goal is to enhance LLMs with SAP’s explicit semantics to enhance AI services like Joule and agents,” said Pavithra G K, head of Business Knowledge Graphs, SAP Business AI. The graph is meant to serve as a toolkit, a tool-discovery mechanism, and a framework for planning and reasoning in agent-based scenarios.
